title: Malaysia & Singapore, from the Malay and Chinese press

stories.text: Malaysia's Prisons Department is in the final stage of setting the conditions for Najib's house arrest.
Singapore's PSI in the west rose to 230, the highest reading this year.
Schools in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang and Penang reopen on Monday.
Malaysia is considering sending helicopters and water-bombing aircraft to help Indonesia.
Only 9 per cent of homes are affordable for households earning RM6,000.
Melaka state election: Barisan Nasional will announce its candidates on 28 October.
Melaka state election: Pejuang hopes to contest one or two seats.
The E-Commerce Bill will be tabled in Parliament next year.
Malaysia's Finance Ministry dismissed a rumour, saying no service charge is being imposed on QR code payments.
stories.source: Sin Chew Daily 星洲日报

stories.text: More than 300 female students have been victims of AI-generated nude images.
The government is working to speed up death certificates for 54 Malaysians missing in Nepal.
After complaints about RON95 petrol quality, Caltex is collecting fuel samples from affected vehicles for testing.
With the Budget boosting social protection, 1.2 million employees are being urged to rejoin the LINDUNG 24 scheme.
Haze has hit the Deepavali bazaar in Singapore's Little India, and organisers may seek subsidies to help stallholders.
A Singapore parliamentary delegation is visiting three places in Europe to strengthen parliamentary links and bilateral cooperation.
